newsitem.title: USA: Dow industrials lower at midday, NYSE resets curbs.
newsitem.headline: Dow industrials lower at midday, NYSE resets curbs.

text.p: The Dow industrials were lower at midday Thursday, weighed down by a sell-off in shares of IBM. The decline triggered the NYSE's curbs on index-arbitrage trades for the second time today at 1223 EST/1723 GMT.

Analysts said they expected the market to remain defensive ahead of the release of the March employment report tomorrow, one of the indicators investors are watching to get a clue as to further Fed action on rates.
The Dow fell 52 points, or 0.81 percent, to 6465. Losers led gainers by 15 to eight on volume of 259 million shares.
U.S. Treasuries were down, with the long bond off 4/32 to yield 7.08 percent.

The Nasdaq Composite Index was up six points at 1207, reflecting a rally in high techs in the face of the sell-off in International Business Machines Corp, which was down 3-3/8 at 130-3/8 after having sunk as low as 128-7/8.

"It's nice to see the techs rally despite IBM weakness. Generally, though, the market is very, very weak," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp. "There is pressure on portfolio managers to raise cash either in response to redemptions or in anticipation of redemptions."
Johnson said, "Managers have to protect portfolios. Some call it momentum investing. I call it a good defence."

The market got off to a weak start with IBM leading the Dow sharply lower, first triggering NYSE curbs at 1010 EST/1510 GMT. A slight bounce in the bond market helped the average recoup some it losses leading to curbs being lifted at 1149 EST/1649 GMT.
"You have a fluctuating Dow because the mood has changed on Wall Street," Johnson said. "We have moved from the perception of a goldilocks economy to fears of a boom-and-bust economy."
He said the next two employment reports will be closely watched for indications of whether the economy is accelerating.

While IBM remained weak, over-the-counter high techs rallied. Cisco Systems Inc, the most actively traded Nasdaq issue, was up 5/8 at 48-1/8. Intel Corp was up 1-3/8 at 138-3/8 and Microsoft Corp was up two at 94.

"This is a good sign," Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said. "At least the weakness in IBM has not caused other technology stocks to fall. That indicates to me that we have probably seen the lows in the tech stocks.
IBM tumbled on renewed fears that currency translations and a mainframe product transition will hurt its first quarter earnings, analysts and traders said.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column today highlighted the actions about two weeks ago by a few analysts who cut their earnings estimates on IBM.
Lucent Technologies Inc rose 1-3/4 to 51-7/8 after the company told analysts it had cut internal costs and expects strong second-quarter sales in its software and wireless divisions.
Dean Witter Reynolds said it upgraded HBO & Co to buy from accumulate based on valuation. HBO was up 3-15/16 at 47-9/16.
